counterexample_or_failure_condition: A test whose child process bypasses the bootstrap (python -I or -S, git, shell) writes under the documentation root outside an open wave folder during a run, and the run records a passing receipt.
expected: If Requirement 3 held as written, every write under docs/ would be refused in the worker, including from child processes.
known_bad_detection_method: Guarded write to docs/plans/new.md refused in the same probe (positive control), so the successful bypass writes are not an artifact of an uninstalled guard.
limitations: Probe ran on a scratch fixture with the live guard module, not a full suite run; the count of tests whose children write under docs is not established.
observed: docs/plans/new.md REFUSED; docs/agents/session-handoff.md, docs/workflow-config.json and docs/new.md WRITTEN; the python -I child wrote docs/plans/raw.md. The docstring at run_tests.py:611-612 states the refusal is not isolation against native or bootstrap-bypassing writes. Tests spawn -I/-S children (test_runtime_advisory.py:147, test_setup_readiness_integration.py:31/74/202/215, test_history_paths.py:96, test_review_evidence.py:328). The existing control tests/test_run_tests_repo_guard.py:737-742 relies on the end-of-run guard to catch exactly such an -I write to docs/waves/1abcd example/events.jsonl, a folder with no open wave record.
proposition: 23nqu Requirement 1 tolerates any change under the documentation root outside an open wave's folder, while Requirement 3 assumes the in-worker write refusal can be extended to cover every test write there; the refusal is a Python audit hook installed through a sitecustomize bootstrap and cannot cover native, isolated (-I/-S) or pre-opened-descriptor writes, so end-of-run detection of those writes is lost.

safety_and_authorization: Read-only against the repository; probe wrote only into a scratch fixture that was deleted afterwards.

disposition_rationale: The plan's central protection claim (Requirement 3, AC-3) is not achievable for bypassing writers; the plan must state the limit and keep detection for those writes or narrow Requirement 1 before implementation.

observed: By the plan's own Requirement 9.3, in the window the status still shows delivery approvals current while review and close are blocked as stale; Requirement 8 keeps 'not receipt-bound' on those rows. Close cannot proceed in the window, so the reported harm (closing with no delivery review of late changes) is prevented.
proposition: Intent gap behind the partially verdict for 23q1g: between a late admission and the next re-Prepare, the review status row of every delivery approval still reads approved, with the unchanged phrase 'not receipt-bound', although the wave then holds a change no delivery approval covered. The Product Intent says an approval shown as current was recorded when the wave already held every change it holds now; in that window the readable row says otherwise, and only the separate review_policy_receipt_stale diagnostic and the review and close blocks tell the reader.
public_path: wf_add_change then wf_review_wave(phase='implementation') or the persisted wave.md status block, before re-Prepare
safety_and_authorization: Read-only review; no repository edit.

disposition_rationale: Close is already blocked while the receipt is stale, so authority is unaffected and the residual is the readability of the status row in a bounded window. Closing it needs the projection to read the admitted change list from the wave record, or a receipt at admission, which is a design change; it is disclosed in Requirement 9.3 and carried to the operator as an open decision.
promotion_trigger: Evidence that an operator or agent acted on an approved delivery row during the window, or that any path other than the stale-receipt-gated review and close consumes delivery approval currency.
